guide:
## Overview

[FLUX 3 Image Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein)
is a 5.6B distilled image transformer from Black Forest Labs for text-to-image
generation and image editing (single- and multi-reference). It uses
Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct as the text encoder and runs a fixed 16-step schedule
with no classifier-free guidance. vLLM-Omni serves it through an
OpenAI-compatible API:

| Mode | Endpoint | Request body |
|------|----------|--------------|
| T2I | `/v1/images/generations` | JSON (`prompt`, `size`, `seed`) |
| I2I | `/v1/chat/completions` | Chat message with the reference image as a base64 data URI |

The checkpoint is a single package: DiT (`model.safetensors`), image
autoencoder (`ae.safetensors`), and `text_encoder/` at the root, with
quantized DiT packages under `variants/fp8r` and `variants/nvfp4`. Select a
variant with
`--stage-overrides '{"0":{"additional_config":{"variant":"fp8r"}}}'`; omit it
for the BF16 root package.

## Prerequisites

- Accept the [FLUX Kommunity License](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein/blob/main/LICENSE.md) on Hugging Face, then `hf auth login`. The license permits non-commercial use with a commercial-output exception for Qualifying Users.
- Recommended: use the day-0 Docker image `vllm/vllm-omni:flux-3-image-klein`, which ships vLLM-Omni and all dependencies. Bare-metal installs use vLLM-Omni from source (see Install above).

## Launching the server

With the day-0 image:

```bash
docker run --runtime nvidia --gpus all \
  -v ${HF_HOME:-$HOME/.cache/huggingface}:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  --env "HF_TOKEN=$HF_TOKEN" \
  -p 8099:8099 \
  --ipc=host \
  vllm/vllm-omni:flux-3-image-klein \
  vllm serve black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein --omni \
    --served-model-name flux-3-image-klein \
    --port 8099
```

Bare metal:

```bash
vllm serve black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein --omni \
  --served-model-name flux-3-image-klein \
  --port 8099

# FP8R / NVFP4 DiT variant
vllm serve black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein --omni \
  --served-model-name flux-3-image-klein \
  --stage-overrides '{"0":{"additional_config":{"variant":"fp8r"}}}' \
  --port 8099
```

Useful extras (see `examples/online_serving/flux3/run_server.sh` in the vLLM-Omni repository):

- `--tensor-parallel-size N` / `--cfg-parallel-size N` for multi-GPU scaling.
- `--fp8-attention` (FlashInfer/cuDNN FP8 DiT attention, SM100 only, needs cuDNN >= 9.17.1).
- `--lora-path /path/to/adapter --lora-scale 1.0` to preload a PEFT LoRA adapter; each request still selects the adapter by path.
- `uv pip install -e '.[prims-ts]'` enables PrimsTS kernels for FP8R/NVFP4 packages on SM100/SM103/SM107; BF16 always uses vLLM kernels.

## Offline inference

```bash
# T2I
python examples/offline_inference/flux3/end2end.py \
  --model black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein \
  --prompt "a serene alpine meadow at golden hour, wildflowers in the foreground"

# I2I (conditioning image; repeat --image for multi-reference, up to 10)
python examples/offline_inference/flux3/end2end.py \
  --model black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein \
  --image /absolute/path/to/reference.png \
  --prompt "restyle as a watercolor painting with soft pastel tones" \
  --seed 7
```

## Prompt upsampling (optional)

[black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup)
is a Qwen3.5-9B vision-language fine-tune that expands a short request into
the detailed caption FLUX 3 Image Klein works best with — the reference
inference code runs it in front of the image model by default. It is a
standard `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` checkpoint, so it is served with
the stock vLLM image on a separate GPU:

```bash
hf download black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup --local-dir /path/to/pup

docker run --gpus '"device=0"' --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /path/to/pup:/model:ro \
  vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0 \
  --model /model \
  --served-model-name flux-3-image-klein-pup \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3
```

The system prompts (`system_prompts.json` in the pup repo) select
text-to-image vs. editing mode, and `t2i_bbox` / `i2i_bbox` variants return
the caption plus a JSON table of `[y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max]` boxes on the
0-1000 grid. A ready-made client is `openai_client_pup.py` next to
`openai_client.py` in `examples/online_serving/flux3/` of the vLLM-Omni
repository — pass `--image` repeatedly (up to 10) for multi-reference
editing; feed its printed caption to the image model as the prompt.

## Behavior and constraints

- **Distilled package**: do not pass `guidance_scale` or a nonempty
  `negative_prompt` — the model rejects them. Step count and flow shift
  default to the package config (16 steps, shift 6.93); `--steps` and
  `--flow-shift` override them.
- **Multi-reference editing**: I2I accepts up to 10 reference images, sent
  in order as multiple `image_url` entries in the chat message. Prompts can
  cite them by position ("the first image", "the second image", ...).
- **I2I has no strength parameter**: the reference image is fed to the DiT as
  conditioning tokens and generation always starts from pure noise. The seed
  controls how far the output drifts from the reference — some seeds stay
  very close to the input, so change the seed when you want a bolder restyle.
- Startup logs show two benign `Error parsing config ... Should have a
  'model_type' key` lines: the package's root `config.json` is a custom FLUX
  format, and vLLM-Omni falls back to the Flux3 pipeline automatically.
- Bounding boxes on a 0-1000 grid can be embedded in the prompt to place,
  move, recolor, or remove elements (see the model card).

## Verified setup

Recipe validated end-to-end on 2026-10-15 with the day-0 image build
(arm64, CUDA 13.0) on a GB200: T2I 1024x1024 in ~2.1s and I2I in ~2.8s
after a ~105s engine startup; ~19 GiB GPU memory with the BF16 package.
